Author: @LizardSkynyrd
Content:
I used to work for the Federal Bureau of Prisons, and I can say that prison camps especially minimum security ones are often more like summer camps than traditional prisons. Most don’t even have fences and operate with significantly fewer guards.

There are typically three daily counts where the “campers” (we weren’t allowed to call them inmates) have to line up and be accounted for. But in between those counts, they’re free to walk outside, use outdoor recreation areas, or hang out in the rec rooms. The only real limitations are posted signs indicating areas that are off limits.

The camp I worked at was surrounded by woods near an interstate, and families would often drop off items in the woods for pickup. With minimal staff and surveillance, things like fast food, air fryers, and other contraband would find their way in. I remember during a small shakedown, we found 48 cell phones in just two hours and that was without a full search.
